name: Museum im Ballhaus Imst
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum in the Ballhaus in Imst: historical 16th-century grain and bale storage with Imst town history, sacred art, and the famous Schemenlaufen carnival.
beschreibung:
Overview

The traditional Museum in the Ballhaus is located in the historic town center of Imst, the district capital in the Tyrolean Oberland, at Ballgasse 1, at an altitude of approximately 830 meters. Housed in one of the town's most imposing and architecturally significant secular buildings – a monumental, listed storage building from the first half of the 16th century – the museum forms the cultural memory of the Imst valley basin. Across several modern exhibition floors, the house offers fascinating insights into the town's over 700-year history, ancient trade and crafts, and the world-famous Tyrolean carnival traditions.

Route & Requirements

The monumental building was erected around 1530 as a municipal granary and bale storage (warehouse for cloth bales and trade goods along the transit route). In 2003, this historic building was transformed into a contemporary town museum, preserving its historical structure, including massive wooden beam ceilings and solid rubble stone walls. An absolute highlight of the exhibition is the section dedicated to the Imster Schemenlaufen: this traditional carnival is one of the oldest and most spectacular customs in the Alps and was the first Austrian custom to be included in the worldwide UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2012.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum in the Ballhaus Imst is open year-round: Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM, and Saturdays from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM (closed on Sundays and public holidays; special guided tours for groups are possible at any time upon request). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults approx. €5.00, seniors and students approx. €4.00, children and teenagers under 18 years enjoy free admission! With the regional Imst Guest Card, admission is free.

Tips

The historic Ballhaus has been exemplarily renovated to be barrier-free: thanks to a modern glass elevator, all floors and exhibition rooms are accessible without thresholds for wheelchair users and strollers. Combine your museum visit with a stroll along the Imster Brunnenweg or through the wild and romantic Rosengartenschlucht gorge, whose entrance is just a few minutes' walk from the museum. The town of Imst also offers numerous charming cafés and restaurants, inviting you to linger after your museum visit. Inform yourself in advance about possible special exhibitions that may take place throughout the year, offering additional insights into specific themes of Imst's history and providing multifaceted perspectives on the rich urban art and cultural history of the Imst region.
